channel.title: n8n release notes: editor and nodes
channel.description: Feature-level updates from n8n releases: what shipped in the editor and the integration nodes.

item.title: Replace Windsurf with Devin in the MCP client dialog
item.description: The instance-level MCP "Connect a client" dialog now offers Devin instead of Windsurf (renamed Devin Desktop by Cognition), with an updated official icon and correct position in the IDE group. Selecting Devin shows the shared config file path (~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json) and a copyable mcpServers entry using HTTP transport, matching both the Devin CLI and desktop app configuration formats. No one-click setup button is available for Devin.

item.title: Add Antigravity to the MCP client connection dialog
item.description: The MCP client connection dialog now includes Antigravity in the IDE group, with its own color icon shown in the dropdown and selected-client button. Selecting it displays a copyable mcpServers config snippet with the instance server URL, plus setup steps pointing to ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json, noting that the Antigravity IDE, desktop app, and agy CLI share this file. Gemini CLI remains unchanged in the CLI group.

item.title: Show who created each preference on the Preferences page
item.description: The Preferences page in Settings > Context now shows a 'Created by' column instead of 'Source'. It displays the name of the user who created each preference, with the origin noted in parentheses for preferences added via the n8n assistant or MCP (e.g. 'Jane Doe (MCP)'). If the user no longer exists, only the origin is shown. The MCP label was also renamed from 'Connected AI tool' to 'MCP'.

item.title: Add project selection to Vertex AI credentials
item.description: Google Vertex AI credentials now let you pick a Google Cloud project from a dropdown populated via your service account, or select Custom to enter a Project ID manually. Manual entry remains available while the list loads or if lookup fails. The credential's connection test now checks whichever project (selected or custom) the node will actually use for requests.

item.title: Add Google Vertex AI credentials
item.description: Added a new Google Vertex AI credential type with a Project ID field, usable alongside existing Google Service Account credentials in the Vertex AI Chat Model and Embeddings nodes. Selecting it uses the credential's project for requests, while a node-level Region setting still overrides the credential's Region. The credential includes a connection test that verifies project access via the Vertex AI locations endpoint.

item.title: Recommend Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 models in AI Assistant setup
item.description: The AI Assistant setup model picker now suggests newer models by default: Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 for Anthropic, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra for OpenAI, and updated equivalents for OpenRouter, with the first option in each provider marked as Recommended. Existing instances keep their previously saved model, and the default instance AI model environment variable is unchanged.

item.title: Show the restriction callout and lock the agent tool configuration form
item.description: When an agent tool's node type is blocked by an instance or project policy, opening it in the agent builder now shows a callout explaining the restriction with a link to contact instance admins. The configuration form is locked read-only (parameters, credentials, approval setting, title), Save is disabled, but the tool can still be removed so the agent can be fixed and published.

item.title: Google Gemini Node: Show Nano Banana 2.1 and 2 Lite in the image model list
item.description: The Google Gemini node's Image Generate model list now correctly includes Nano Banana 2.1 and Nano Banana 2 Lite models, which were previously hidden because their model IDs don't contain the word "image". The dropdown now shows friendly labels for these models while keeping them out of text and audio model lists.

item.title: Explain instance-role access in the credential sharing "Used in" row
item.description: In the credential Sharing tab, the "Used in" row for your own personal project now clarifies access when your instance role (Owner, admin, or custom role) lets you use any credential. It shows "Can use in personal space" with a tooltip explaining you can already use the credential there without a share, while the Share button's tooltip clarifies that sharing additionally grants access in team projects.

item.title: Add order to settings sidebar links
item.description: Settings sidebar links now support an optional order field, letting the shell and installed modules (like MCP, Chat Hub, Instance AI, and Agents) position their links precisely relative to each other instead of relying on manual insertion logic. This is an internal, developer-facing improvement for module authors; the visible sidebar order for end users is unchanged.

item.title: Animate the n8n Assistant activity indicator
item.description: The n8n Assistant's activity indicator while it edits an agent has been refreshed. It now shows a new animated grid spinner, a colorful animated glow beneath the editor, and a status label that cycles through playful words like 'Imagining…' and 'Tinkering…' every five seconds. Panel headings and row labels dim while changes are in progress. Animations respect reduced-motion settings.

item.title: Sort the credential sharing list by people, then projects
item.description: The credential sharing modal now lists people first, then projects, each sorted alphabetically, instead of grouping by access. Projects the credential is only used in (not yet shared) now appear inline with shared ones rather than in a separate block, and keep their position when the owner shares the credential with them, making the list easier to follow. Requires the N8N_ENV_FEAT_CRED_SHARING flag.

item.title: Azure OpenAI Chat Model Node: Rename the Foundry nodes and credentials to Microsoft Foundry
item.description: The Azure Chat Model and Embeddings nodes, along with their API Key and Entra ID credentials, are now labeled 'Microsoft Foundry' to match Microsoft's rebranded platform name. This is a display-only change: node and credential types, saved workflows, and existing credentials continue to work unchanged, and the old names (Azure, Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry, AOAI) still work as search aliases in the node panel.

item.title: Add a state column to the migration rule detail
item.description: The migration rule detail page now shows a State column with an inline Open / Won't fix picker for each affected workflow. Marking a finding Won't fix removes it from the overview and affected-workflow counts without unpublishing the workflow; it automatically reopens as Open if the scan detects the issue again, and is marked fixed once resolved.

item.title: Azure AI Foundry Chat Model Node: Speak the Anthropic Messages schema for Claude deployments
item.description: The Azure AI Foundry Chat Model node now supports Claude deployments by speaking the Anthropic Messages API, using existing API key or Entra ID credentials. A new Model Family setting lets users switch between OpenAI and Anthropic, with appropriate temperature limits and accurate token usage reporting for Claude. Classic credentials are rejected early with a clear error, since they only support the OpenAI route.

item.title: Rebuild the personal settings page with the design-system settings components
item.description: The Personal settings page has been redesigned using n8n's shared design-system components, matching the look of instance settings pages. It now shows inline field validation, clearer locked-field explanations for SSO, LDAP, and environment-managed accounts, and an improved theme selector with icons. Change password, 2FA setup, and password/2FA confirmation dialogs were rebuilt with better layouts and now show inline errors instead of closing on failed attempts. New monitor and moon icons were added.

item.title: Configure workflow tool inputs for Agents
item.description: Agent workflow tools now have an Advanced section to configure each workflow input individually: let the AI fill it with optional guidance, set a fixed value, or use an expression. 'Return all node outputs' moved into this section. The editor reuses familiar parameter and expression controls from the node editor, and configured inputs are validated and preserved across saves, reopens, version restores, and Wait continuations.

item.title: Add agent setup checklist
item.description: The agent builder now shows a 'Finish setup' checklist that highlights remaining configuration steps, helping users distinguish genuine errors from unconfigured fields. It lists incomplete tasks, moves completed ones to the end, and lets users jump directly to related model, instructions, tool, channel, and publish controls. The panel can be minimized and peeked at on hover.

item.title: Embeddings Azure OpenAI Node: Add Entra ID authentication
item.description: The Microsoft Foundry Embeddings (Azure OpenAI) node now supports Microsoft Entra ID (OAuth2) authentication as an alternative to API keys, matching the existing chat model node. Enterprises that disallow stored API keys can now use Azure OpenAI embeddings by selecting Entra ID authentication, which works with both classic and Foundry deployment endpoints.

item.title: Show whose credential a node uses and let others switch from it
item.description: When a node uses a credential you can't access, the credential picker now shows whose credential it is, marks it as unavailable, and explains why via a tooltip. You can switch the node to a credential you can use, unlocking its parameters so you can edit and save your changes. This is available behind the N8N_ENV_FEAT_CRED_SHARING feature flag; editor behavior is unchanged when it's off.

item.title: Databricks Node: Enable the Job resource
item.description: The Databricks node now exposes a Job resource in its resource selector, enabling four previously hidden operations: Run, Get Job, Get Run, and Get Run Output. These operations and their logic already existed in the node but were not selectable in the UI; this change makes them visible and usable in workflows targeting Databricks jobs.

item.title: Add Stop all tasks to the Preview task panel
item.description: The Preview task panel now includes a Stop all tasks control next to View trace, letting users cancel running background sub-agent tasks. Rows show a Stopping… state until each task reaches a checkpoint, then Stopped, disappearing together once the group finishes. Progress persists across reloads, failed stop requests keep rows visible with a retryable error, and keyboard focus is restored when the stop control disappears.

item.title: Add activation menus to Agent capabilities
item.description: You can now activate or deactivate individual capabilities in the standalone Agent Builder, including skills, custom tools, node tools, workflow references, sub-agents, and schedules, directly from each item's context menu. Deactivated items stay visible and editable, keep their configuration, and are skipped during validation and runtime without appearing in errors. Schedule activation moved from the modal switch into the item menu.

item.title: Allow reordering queued messages in Agent Preview
item.description: You can now reorder queued messages in Agent Preview chat. Drag the handle (or use Up/Down arrow keys) to change which pending message runs next. The order is saved and survives reload, while the active execution and accepted steer messages stay fixed, and live output is preserved when turns run in a different order.

item.title: Add Remove context menus to Agent configuration
item.description: You can now right-click or long-press configuration chips in the Agent setup to quickly remove tools, workflow references, MCP servers, sub-agents, skills, channels, and schedules via a new Remove action. Removing a grouped tool deletes all its members in one step, while removing a dropdown item removes only that tool. Shared workflows and sub-agents stay intact, and existing edit locks, modal controls, and managed Slack confirmations continue to work as before.

item.title: Supabase Node: Add OAuth credentials and reuse them for MCP
item.description: The Supabase node now supports OAuth2 authentication alongside existing API key credentials. When using OAuth2, you select a Supabase project and n8n automatically manages a dedicated Data API secret key, reusing it across runs and refreshing it if it becomes invalid. Node parameter order was updated to show Resource and Operation first. Supabase OAuth2 credentials can also be used to enable the Supabase MCP server in the AI Assistant tools list.

item.title: Add usage and budget settings for agents
item.description: Agent settings now include a Usage and limits card showing current monthly spend, a configurable monthly budget, and a session spend cap. Budgets must be set above 0 to take effect; clearing them disables the guardrail. An optional alert threshold (10-100%) can warn as spend approaches the monthly budget. In the builder preview, hitting a cap or alert shows a card letting you increase the cap or dismiss the alert without stopping the run; published chats are unaffected.

item.title: Stop Execute and Publish when a credential is not yours to use
item.description: The editor now disables Execute and Publish before you click when a workflow uses a credential you don't have permission to use, instead of letting the action fail on the server afterward. The disabled controls name the credential and its owner, and explain that you can still edit and save the workflow or switch to a usable credential. This is gated behind the N8N_ENV_FEAT_CRED_SHARING environment variable.

item.title: Refine the workflow review detail layout
item.description: Improved the workflow review detail page layout: a consistent divider now runs under the inbox and detail tabs, the activity column is centered and capped at 720px wide (Changes tab stays full width), and the metadata panel and activity feed now scroll together as one area so metadata and the comment input stay visible. Also fixed long names/emails wrapping, added spacing from scrollbars, and removed a stray timeline line.

item.title: Show migration progress on report overview
item.description: The Migration report in Settings now shows a progress bar at the top, displaying the share of workflows compatible with the target version along with a "{compatible} of {total} compatible" label. Workflow counts throughout the report are now formatted with locale-aware number formatting for better readability. The bar is also accessible, with proper progressbar roles and ARIA attributes.

item.title: Crypto Node: Add RSA-OAEP hash option
item.description: The Crypto node's asymmetric encrypt/decrypt operations now let you choose the RSA-OAEP hash algorithm, supporting SHA-256 (default, preserving existing workflow behavior) or SHA-1. This enables interoperability with systems that require SHA-1 for OAEP padding when encrypting or decrypting with RSA keys.

item.title: Tell the AI Assistant which preview tabs are open
item.description: The AI Assistant now only sees the preview tabs you currently have open, including which one is active, instead of every artifact ever produced in the thread. Closing tabs is reflected to the assistant, so it won't reference artifacts you've closed unless you explicitly ask about them. This gives more accurate, up-to-date context without affecting prompt caching.

item.title: Release Browser Use to all users
item.description: Browser Use in the n8n Assistant is now available to all users, controlled by the instance admin setting N8N_INSTANCE_AI_BROWSER_USE_ENABLED (on by default) rather than an experiment. It remains unavailable on phones and tablets, including iPads in desktop mode. The experimental "Set up automatically" credential setup option is now disabled by default for all users, with its underlying code kept in place for a possible future return.

item.title: Reorder AI Assistant tabs by dragging
item.description: You can now reorder the preview tabs in the AI Assistant by dragging them sideways, similar to browser tabs. Press and drag a tab past a neighboring tab to swap positions; the other tabs slide aside, and the new order is saved automatically for the thread. Pressing Escape or cancelling the drag restores the original order, and a simple click still selects a tab without reordering it.

item.title: Open any project resource as an AI Assistant tab
item.description: In the AI Assistant, you can now open a new tab for any workflow, data table, or agent in the thread's project directly from a preview tab bar. A new tab button opens a searchable menu scoped to the thread's project, listing recently edited resources (already-open ones are filtered out) or search results. Picking a resource opens it as the active tab, and the choice is saved across reloads.

item.title: Close AI Assistant tabs and keep the open tabs per thread
item.description: You can now close preview tabs in the AI Assistant. Each tab shows a close button on hover or focus, and middle-click or Delete also close a tab. Closing the active tab selects the next (or previous) tab, and closing the last tab closes the preview. Open tabs, closed artifacts, and the active tab are now saved per thread, so they're restored when you reopen it. Closed artifacts reopen automatically if referenced again from chat or the artifacts list.

item.title: Azure OpenAI Chat Model Node: Add the deployment dropdown
item.description: The Azure OpenAI Chat Model node now lets you pick a deployment from a dropdown list instead of typing its name, avoiding typos that previously caused a DeploymentNotFound error. New nodes default to version 1.1, offering 'From List' and 'By ID' modes. The list requires an Azure AI Foundry credential with a Project set; classic credentials or empty projects show a clear error message. Existing version 1 nodes keep their text field and saved values unchanged.

item.title: Submit selected project changes from the promote modal
item.description: You can now select specific project changes and promote them from the promote modal, which previously had a disabled Promote button. On success, a toast confirms how many workflows were pushed and to which branch. If selected workflows have moved to another project, promotion fails with a clear error listing the affected workflows, since selective pushes can't move workflows across projects. This is an enterprise feature requiring promotions and source control to be enabled.

item.title: Show the trigger icon on the execute button and run a trigger from its menu
item.description: The canvas Execute button has been redesigned: it now simply reads "Execute" and shows the selected trigger's icon instead of a second "from [trigger name]" line, with the trigger name still shown in a tooltip. Choosing a trigger from the dropdown now immediately runs the workflow and sets it as the default trigger. The button is now a consistent height, so adjacent Stop buttons no longer resize. The Builder chat uses the same updated component.

item.title: Hide generated AI tools listed in NODES_EXCLUDE and empty node creator entries
item.description: NODES_EXCLUDE now lets you hide a generated AI tool variant (e.g. microsoftOutlookTool) without removing its base node. Additionally, the node creator panel now hides subcategories or views (like 'Other AI Nodes' or 'Other ways...') that have no browsable nodes left, based on NODES_INCLUDE/NODES_EXCLUDE settings, keeping the panel cleaner for restricted instances.

item.title: Replace severity with impact categories in the migration report
item.description: The migration report now shows clearer impact labels instead of low/medium/critical severities: Upgrade blocked, Executions fail, Behavior changes, and Capability removed. Each breaking-change rule has been reclassified based on its actual runtime effect, with color-coded badges and tooltips explaining each category. Rules are now sorted by severity of impact, with blockers shown first and removed capabilities last, making it easier to prioritize fixes before upgrading.

item.title: Add keyboard controls to n8n Assistant panel
item.description: You can now open and close the n8n Assistant panel in the Agent builder using Cmd+J (macOS) or Ctrl+J (Windows/Linux). Escape also closes the panel when focus is inside its input, and the close button now shows an Escape hint. Other canvas shortcuts remain disabled while typing in inputs.

item.title: Open and collapse the logs panel around runs in the AI Assistant artifact view
item.description: In the AI Assistant artifact view, the logs panel now opens automatically when a workflow run starts and collapses on success, staying open if the run fails. It respects a user's manual collapse for the rest of the thread, won't auto-open in small panes, and keeps its own height and open state separate from the main editor's logs panel.

item.title: Show Gateway credits promotions on community nodes
item.description: n8n now displays Gateway credits promotions for eligible community nodes, shown as a callout in the node creator, the NDV, and the credential modal. The promotion text is sourced dynamically and only appears while Gateway credits support the node and the current time falls within the promotion's active window, disappearing automatically once it expires.

item.title: Group the node credential picker by where each credential comes from
item.description: The node credential picker now groups credentials by where they come from, showing personal credentials under 'Available to you' and project or instance-shared credentials under headings like 'Available in [project name]' or 'Available to everyone'. Empty groups are hidden and search filtering respects the groups. This is only active when granular credential sharing (N8N_ENV_FEAT_CRED_SHARING) is enabled; otherwise the dropdown looks unchanged.

item.title: Suggest Gateway credit services during node discovery
item.description: The AI assistant's node suggestion feature now also surfaces relevant n8n Connect Gateway credit services, such as Firecrawl, PDF.co, Brave Search, and LlamaParse, when recommending nodes by category. Previously these services were only found via search or list actions. This applies to assistant chat, workflow building, and agent building, helping users discover credential-free options for web search, scraping, and document parsing.

item.title: Restyle AI Assistant tab bar and add a tab hover card
item.description: Redesigned the AI Assistant's preview tab bar with an updated look, and added a hover card for each tab. The card shows the tab's full name, and for workflows also displays the last edited time and a Published/Draft status, while data table tabs show the edited time and column count. Details load efficiently via batched requests and refresh in the background. Closing tabs and the new tab button are not yet included.

item.title: Azure OpenAI Chat Model Node: Rename to Azure AI Foundry Chat Model
item.description: The 'Azure OpenAI Chat Model' node has been renamed to 'Azure AI Foundry Chat Model' to better reflect that it supports the full Azure AI Foundry catalogue (including Llama, Mistral, Cohere, DeepSeek, Grok and Claude models), not just OpenAI models. Existing workflows are unaffected, and searching for 'Azure OpenAI' still finds the node thanks to a new alias.

item.title: Improve Agent Builder intro interactions
item.description: The Agent Builder intro's template list has been refined: rows now use accessible, semantic markup with keyboard support (Tab, Enter, Space), a hover-revealed arrow indicator, subtle staged fade-and-blur animation, and cleaner spacing and text sizing. Redundant action buttons were removed since rows themselves are now clickable, improving usability for both mouse and keyboard/screen-reader users.

item.title: Group canvas toolbar buttons in a single container
item.description: The canvas toolbar buttons—zoom controls (bottom-left) and canvas actions (top-right)—are now grouped into a single visual container with a shared background, rounded corners, and shadow, instead of appearing as separate floating buttons. This saves canvas space and gives a cleaner, more unified look in both the editor and the node creator panel, in light and dark mode.
